column1: # Verbs and the prepositions they select, from the lists of prepositional verbs in
# R. Huddleston, "The clause: complements", ch. 4 of R. Huddleston and G. K. Pullum,
# The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language (Cambridge University Press, 2002),
# section 6.1.2, with the examples of specified prepositions in section 1.2 [12].
# Transcribed from a 2009 revision draft of the chapter; section numbers are the draft's.
# The book calls the lists "a small sample"; they are not a complete lexicon.
# Columns: lemma, preposition, structure, marks, section.
#   structure  I    verb [prep + O]            refer [to her book]
#              II   verb O [prep + O]          intend it [for Kim]
#              III  verb [prep + O] [prep + O] look [to her] [for guidance]
#              IV   verb [as + PC]             count [as too short]
#              V    verb O [as + PC]           regard it [as successful]
#              VI   verb [prep + O] [as + PC]  think [of it] [as indispensable]
#   marks      -p   the prepositional passive is unacceptable
#              f    fossilised: the preposition is fixed in position
# British spellings are the book's; American ones (categorize, install ...) are added.
# CGEL counts all of these PPs as complements.
